title: Restore a slipped Bowden tube on a robot hand
justification: Repairs the sheath reaction path of a documented tendon-driven robotic end effector, using the Yeah Hand v1.3 design and its actual tube seats.
instruction: Restore the finger’s opening and closing motion.
fault: Proposed: index-extension PTFE tube end displaced laterally from its source-defined seat while the intact tendon still passes through it. The actual loss of travel and absence of self-reseating must be demonstrated before treating this as a valid fault.
objects: Full-scale left-side hand on its ISO robot flange in a buildable service mount
Actual printed skeleton, phalanges, antagonistic spools and cover geometry
PTFE tube OD3mm ID1.5mm per source BOM;0.75mm HERCULES tendon
Ordinary source-specified hand tools; no custom gripping tabs
skill: Support/slacken the tendon path and reseat the sheath end under constrained access, restoring reaction support through physical contact.
scoring: Not implemented. Candidate outcome: correct sheath seating plus three reproducible full finger cycles, hands off. Must define externally measurable travel, retention and damage checks after physical feasibility is established.

nearest.difference_to_demonstrate: Split cable-guide retrofit is cable management, not restoration of a sheath compression reaction path.
Timing-belt tension/motor-mount retention; new task must demonstrate displaced sheath load-path repair, not generic tension adjustment.
Guidewire manipulation in enclosed sheath; here the sheath reaction support itself is repaired.

geometry_note: 4mm named Bowden mesh is a Boolean DIFFERENCE operand defining housing voids. Physical tubing remains BOM3mm. Index-extension end seats at CAD coordinates(31.7966,-9.9980,-59.1214) and(17.0069,-20.8767,-121.4789)mm; path control polygon66.8263mm. Nearby tendon passage cutter2.88mm. Do not equate cutter diameter to tube diameter.
risks: Tube may self-seat or remain functional when displaced; demonstrate an actual recovery fault.
3mm tube above2.88mm passage leaves narrow shoulder; actual contact and compliance must be validated.
Sliding tendon and tube reactions must follow continuous mechanics, never a seated-state predicate.
Preserve full-size covers, motors, real access and fixing hardware.
Published tube stiffness/force not yet calibrated.
Read and fulfill hardware CERN-OHL-S-2.0 obligations before distributing derived CAD.
A finite-difference mechanics check does not count as simulation or task validation.
